reader.title: The Empty Land
reader.text: Our alley sits on empty ground, an extension of the Muqattam desert crouching on the horizon. Nothing stood in that wasteland but the Great House, which al-Gabalawi built to defy fear, loneliness and highwaymen. Its high wall encloses a wide expanse, the western half a garden, the eastern half a residence of three storeys.

reader.title: The Summons
reader.text: One day the Endower called his sons to his room in the house that adjoins the garden pavilion. Idris, Abbas, Radwan, Galil and Adham all came, in their silk robes, and stood before him, so awed that they scarcely dared to look his way except by stealth.

prompts: Would you stop at the first murder?

chat.intro: Macbeth is Shakespeare’s shortest tragedy: a brave general hears a prophecy, and ambition does the rest. Where shall we go?

qa.answer: The witches never tell Macbeth to kill. They name a future and let his ambition do the work, which is why readers still argue whether it is fate or choice.
Lady Macbeth pushes the first murder, then is the first to be undone by it. Her sleepwalking scene is the play’s quiet climax.
Most readers say they would stop at the first murder. Macbeth thinks so too, until he is “in blood stepp’d in so far” that going back is as hard as going on. The second step is always easier.
Ambition, guilt and the price of power. Notice how every promise the witches make is true and still destroys him.

reader.title: The Prophecy
reader.text: On a bleak heath after battle, three witches hail Macbeth, a loyal Scottish general, as Thane of Cawdor and as king to come. They tell Banquo that his children will be kings. Macbeth tells himself that if chance will crown him, chance may do it without his help, yet the words settle in his mind like a seed.

reader.title: The Night of the Murder
reader.text: Urged on by Lady Macbeth, who calls his hesitation weakness, Macbeth kills King Duncan, a guest sleeping under his own roof. The crime wins him the throne and costs him his peace. A voice cries that he has murdered sleep.

reader.title: A Crown Built on Blood
reader.text: Fearing the prophecy about Banquo’s heirs, Macbeth has his old friend killed. At the royal feast Banquo’s ghost takes the empty seat, and the king’s composure breaks in front of the whole court.

reader.title: What the Witches Meant
reader.text: Macbeth returns to the witches and is told to fear Macduff, that no man born of woman can harm him, and that he is safe until Birnam Wood climbs Dunsinane Hill. Each promise is true, and each is a trap.

reader.title: The Fall
reader.text: Lady Macbeth walks in her sleep, trying to wash blood from her hands that no one else can see. Soldiers cut branches from Birnam Wood to hide their numbers, and Macduff, born by cesarean, ends the tyrant’s reign.

prompts: هل كنت ستتوقف عند الجريمة الأولى؟
هل الساحرات نبوءة أم إغواء؟
من الأكثر ذنبًا: ماكبث أم زوجته؟

chat.intro: «ماكبث» أقصر مآسي شكسبير: قائد شجاع يسمع نبوءة، ويتكفّل الطموح بالباقي. من أين نبدأ؟

qa.answer: الساحرات لا يأمرن ماكبث بالقتل أبدًا. يسمّين له مستقبلًا ويتركن طموحه يقوم بالعمل، ولهذا ما زال القرّاء يتجادلون: أهو القدر أم الاختيار؟
الليدي ماكبث هي من تدفع نحو الجريمة الأولى، ثم تكون أول من يتحطّم بسببها. مشهد مشيها أثناء النوم هو الذروة الهادئة للمسرحية.
يقول معظم القرّاء إنهم كانوا سيتوقفون عند الجريمة الأولى. وماكبث يظن ذلك أيضًا، حتى يغوص في الدم إلى حدّ يصبح فيه الرجوع صعبًا كالمضيّ. الخطوة الثانية أسهل دائمًا.
الطموح والذنب وثمن السلطة. لاحظ أن كل وعود الساحرات تتحقق، ومع ذلك تدمّره.

reader.title: النبوءة
reader.text: على أرض مقفرة بعد المعركة، تحيّي ثلاث ساحرات ماكبث، القائد الاسكتلندي الوفيّ، بلقب أمير كودور وبملكٍ قادم. وتخبر بانكو بأن أبناءه سيصبحون ملوكًا. يقول ماكبث لنفسه إن الصدفة إن شاءت تتويجه فلن تحتاج إلى مساعدته، لكن الكلمات تستقر في ذهنه كبذرة.

reader.title: ليلة الجريمة
reader.text: بدفعٍ من الليدي ماكبث التي تعدّ ترددّه ضعفًا، يقتل ماكبث الملك دنكن وهو ضيف نائم تحت سقف بيته. تمنحه الجريمة العرش وتسلبه سكينته، ويصرخ صوتٌ بأنه قتل النوم.

reader.title: تاجٌ مبنيّ على الدم
reader.text: خوفًا من النبوءة التي تخصّ ورثة بانكو، يأمر ماكبث بقتل صديقه القديم. وفي المأدبة الملكية يجلس شبح بانكو على المقعد الشاغر، فيفقد الملك رباطة جأشه أمام البلاط كله.

reader.title: ما قصدته الساحرات
reader.text: يعود ماكبث إلى الساحرات فيُقال له أن يحذر ماكداف، وأن لا مولودًا من امرأة يستطيع أذاه، وأنه آمن حتى تتسلق غابة بيرنام تلّ دنسينان. كل وعدٍ صادق، وكل وعدٍ فخّ.

reader.title: السقوط
reader.text: تمشي الليدي ماكبث وهي نائمة محاولةً غسل دمٍ عن يديها لا يراه أحد. يقطع الجنود أغصانًا من غابة بيرنام لإخفاء عددهم، وينهي ماكداف، المولود بعملية قيصرية، حكم الطاغية.

chat.intro: Othello is a tragedy of trust: a respected general, a loyal wife, and one ensign who whispers. Where shall we begin?

qa.answer: Iago gives different reasons at different times, and that is the point: his malice is restless and seeks any excuse. He never forces anyone, he only suggests.

card.s: The ensign who never raises his voice

qa.answer: Jealousy here is built, not born. A lost handkerchief, a half-heard word, and certainty grows from nothing.
The play moves from the order of Venice to the isolation of Cyprus, where the rules loosen and suspicion grows.
Trust, race, jealousy and the danger of certainty. One honest question might have saved everyone.

reader.title: A Secret Marriage
reader.text: In Venice, Othello, a celebrated Moorish general, has married Desdemona against her father’s wishes. The Duke sends him to defend Cyprus from the Turks, and Desdemona sails with him.

reader.title: Iago’s Grudge
reader.text: Passed over for promotion, Iago, Othello’s ensign, decides to destroy him. Everyone calls him honest, and he uses that trust to plant a doubt about Desdemona and the young lieutenant Cassio.

reader.title: The Handkerchief
reader.text: Othello’s first gift to Desdemona, a handkerchief embroidered with strawberries, is stolen by Iago’s wife Emilia and left where Cassio will find it. The small cloth becomes proof of a crime that never happened.

reader.title: Jealousy Takes Hold
reader.text: Othello’s love curdles into rage. He strikes Desdemona in public and demands proof that Iago has already arranged. The more she protests her innocence, the guiltier she seems to him.

reader.title: The Truth, Too Late
reader.text: Othello smothers Desdemona in her bed. Emilia exposes her husband’s lies, but it is too late. Seeing what he has done, Othello speaks of himself as one who loved not wisely but too well, and takes his own life.

تنتقل المسرحية من نظام البندقية إلى عزلة قبرص، حيث تتراخى القواعد ويكبر الشك.

chat.intro: War and Peace follows five aristocratic families through Napoleon’s invasion of Russia, and asks how a life is shaped by history it cannot control. Where to?

qa.answer: Natasha, Pierre and Prince Andrei are the book’s heart: three people who each search for a life that feels true, and find it in different places.
The invasion of 1812 is the book’s turning point, from Austerlitz to the burning of Moscow. Tolstoy argues that no single great man steers events.

card.s: The year that changed every family

qa.answer: Free will against history, family against the state, and the quiet courage of ordinary days.

reader.title: A Moscow Salon, 1805
reader.text: At Anna Pavlovna’s party, the Russian aristocracy argues about Napoleon. Pierre Bezukhov, the awkward illegitimate son of a count, shocks the room with his honesty, while Prince Andrei, weary of society, prepares to leave for war.

reader.title: Natasha
reader.text: Natasha Rostova, bright and impulsive, dances at her first ball and falls in love with life. Love and mistakes follow, including a near-elopement that costs her Prince Andrei’s trust.

reader.title: Austerlitz and Borodino
reader.text: Wounded at Austerlitz, Andrei lies looking at the endless sky and sees how small ambition is. At Borodino, Tolstoy shows that no general commands the chaos: history is moved by countless small acts.

reader.title: Moscow Burns
reader.text: The French occupy Moscow and the city burns. Pierre, taken prisoner, meets the peasant Platon Karataev, whose quiet acceptance of life teaches him what all his searching could not.

reader.title: After the War
reader.text: Families rebuild their lives. Pierre and Natasha marry, and ordinary days of children and conversation matter more than any victory. Tolstoy closes with an essay on free will and the forces that carry us all.

reader.title: A Lonely Dreamer

reader.title: Confessions
reader.text: On the second night he tells her about his dreams, and on the third she tells him about hers. For the first time he is not alone inside his imagination.

reader.title: The Letter
reader.text: He offers to deliver her letter. As they wait for an answer that does not come, she leans on him, and he finds himself hoping against everything he promised.

reader.title: The Morning After
reader.text: On the fourth night the lodger appears, and Nastenka runs to him. The dreamer is left with gratitude and an ache, and with the thought that a whole moment of happiness may be enough for a lifetime.
